summary: Duplicate external webhook/tool executions when TS browser SDK + service worker background sync replays retries across tabs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicated external webhook (third-party accounting webhook) invocations and duplicated tool/function runs when their web app uses the Redwood TypeScript/browser SDK in combination with a service worker background sync. Impact: Duplicate side-effects in third-party systems (double invoices) leading to customer outage of their payment workflow.

Environment/Context: SaaSify is using Redwood TS SDK v1.8.2 in a single-page application deployed on Netlify. They register a service worker that implements Background Sync to retry failed POSTs when the device regains connectivity. Users often have the web app open in multiple tabs on mobile devices with flaky cellular connectivity. The SDK is configured to auto-retry failed streaming requests and to use optimistic local retry logic in the UI.

Observed behavior: When network blips produce 502/504 from the Redwood API or the edge proxy, the browser app performs a local retry and also enqueues a background sync entry via the service worker. If a user has multiple tabs open, each tab enqueues its own background sync event and the service worker dispatches POSTs (containing function/tool call payloads) after the device reconnects. The third-party webhook receives duplicated requests 2–3 times for the same logical action.

Customer expectation: Single effective tool/webhook invocation per user action; guidance on SDK patterns and config to avoid duplicate side effects from client-side background replay and multi-tab scenarios.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy Redwood TS SDK v1.8.2 in an SPA with a registered service worker that uses Background Sync to re-send failed POSTs.
2) Open the SPA in two browser tabs on a mobile device (or in two desktop tabs simulating mobile network flakiness).
3) Trigger a function/tool call that results in a webhook POST (e.g., create-invoice tool).
4) Simulate a brief network outage so the initial request fails with a 502/504.
5) Allow the SDK to perform its client-side optimistic retry while the service worker enqueues a sync event for background retry.
6) Restore network connectivity. The service worker background sync runs and replays the POSTs from each tab, while the SDK retry from the main thread also completes, producing multiple webhook deliveries.
7) Observe duplicate webhook receipts on the third-party endpoint.

HTTP trace (abbreviated):

2026-03-10T14:03:12.130Z - sdk-js retry (client-side) attempt=1 idempotency-key=none
2026-03-10T14:03:14.500Z - ServiceWorker backgroundSync.register(tag=create-invoice:xyz) (tab A)
2026-03-10T14:03:14.507Z - ServiceWorker backgroundSync.register(tag=create-invoice:xyz) (tab B)
2026-03-10T14:03:20.800Z - backgroundSync fired -> POST /callbacks/invoice (tab A payload) -> 200 OK third-party
2026-03-10T14:03:20.805Z - backgroundSync fired -> POST /callbacks/invoice (tab B payload) -> 200 OK third-party
2026-03-10T14:03:21.000Z - sdk-js client retry completes -> POST /callbacks/invoice -> 200 OK third-party

Note: client logs show no Idempotency-Key header being set by application code. SDK v1.8.2 leaves idempotency to caller by default in browser streaming mode.
investigation:
Support reproduced the pattern locally by installing a simple service worker that queues failed POSTs and replaying from two tabs. We confirmed that the browser SDK did not inject an Idempotency-Key header in the outbound tool-calling POSTs in the customer's configuration. Edge logs show three distinct POSTs within ~1s with slightly different client-side timestamps. We verified the service worker queue produced one entry per tab, and the SDK optimistic retry produced a third POST.

We reviewed the current JS SDK behavior: in browser/streaming mode the SDK avoids automatic idempotency header injection to reduce accidental long-lived stored tokens in client storage; in Node it auto-generates per-request Idempotency-Key unless the developer sets one. This design choice reduces risk of persisting keys on disk for server apps but leaves browser devs responsible for idempotency when they use background replay mechanisms.

We also checked that the third-party webhook endpoint accepted identical payloads and had no dedup facility on their side.
hypothesis: Duplicate invocations are caused by the combination of: (a) absence of per-action idempotency key in the client payload, (b) multiple independent background-sync queue entries (one per tab), and (c) concurrent optimistic retries by the main thread. With no cross-tab coordination or shared idempotency token, each replay is treated as a fresh request by Redwood and by the downstream webhook.
workaround:
Short term suggestions provided to customer: 
- Configure the client to generate and attach a stable per-action idempotency token (Idempotency-Key) at the moment of user action and include it in the tool call payload or an Idempotency-Key header. Persist that token in sessionStorage and share via the BroadcastChannel API across tabs to avoid multiple independent background-sync entries.
- Disable optimistic client-side automatic retries in the browser SDK while relying on background sync to replay requests once (SDK config: retries=0 in browser).
- On the webhook/third-party side implement idempotency detection keyed by a user+action+client-token so duplicate POSTs are ignored server-side.

We provided a small sample snippet (TS) demonstrating generating a UUID per user action, saving to sessionStorage, and broadcasting it to other tabs. This was included inline in the support reply.
resolution:
Support provided a two-part resolution on 2026-03-12: 
1) Customer action: SaaSify implemented a per-action Idempotency-Key stored in sessionStorage and shared across tabs via BroadcastChannel. They also disabled SDK optimistic retries in the browser (set clientRetry=0) and relied on single background sync replay. After deployment, duplicate webhook deliveries stopped.
2) Product/SDK change: Engineering opened github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/842 to add opt-in browser automatic idempotency behavior (generate a cryptographically random per-action Idempotency-Key when app supplies a stable action_id or when developer enables 'autoBrowserIdempotency=true'). The PR includes warnings in README and avoids persistent disk storage; auto keys live per-action only and can be surfaced to service workers via a documented BroadcastChannel pattern.

We verified with the customer that the fix eliminated duplicate side-effects for their test cases. Ticket closed after confirming no further duplicates reported for 48 hours.
